$comment: Log-standard gate config, consumed by scripts/check-log-standard.mjs. Two ratchets (exact-equality counts, both directions) and two allowlists (exact per-file, per-symbol counts with a reason). Regenerate the two ratchet numbers with `node scripts/check-log-standard.mjs --write` in the same commit that changes them; the allowlists are edited by hand because a new or removed site needs a human-authored reason, which --write cannot supply.
$comment_scope: getRootLoggerCount and unnamespacedBindingCount are scoped to packages/sdk/src (excluding __tests__, __fixtures__ and *.test.ts). consoleAllowlist and streamWriteAllowlist are scoped to packages/*/src across every package (one directory below packages/ — packages/providers/<name>/src is nested one level deeper and out of scope; see the script's file header).

consoleAllowlist.reason: the dependency direction sdk ← telemetry (AGENTS.md) forbids this package from importing the SDK logger, and this is telemetry's own shutdown error-of-last-resort path — there is no Logger available to it here.

streamWriteAllowlist.reason: createLoggerImpl's own sink — the one place a Logger produced by getRootLogger() actually reaches a stream. Every other production write is expected to go through a Logger, not around one.
JsonFormatter.print — the CLI's user-facing result channel, a deliberately separate host-protocol channel from the structured logger.
JsonFormatter.info/error — the same Formatter's diagnostic-to-stderr half.
TextFormatter.print — same host-protocol channel as JsonFormatter, rendered as text.
TextFormatter.info/error — error() writes the message and, when details are present, the details block as two separate writes.
YamlFormatter.print — same host-protocol channel, rendered as YAML.
the process entrypoint's fatal-error handler, reached when runCli's own promise rejects — before any Logger exists to write through.
the no-TTY notice for interactive mode — a one-line usage message, not a diagnostic.
runCli's top-level catch: a bad-config message and a fatal-error message, both bootstrap-time paths in the same category as bin.ts.
the command's own argument-parsing usage error, printed before a Logger or Formatter is constructed for this invocation.
the doctor command's own report renderer (help text, JSON report, human report) — like run-stream.ts, this command bypasses the shared output/Formatter.

the NDJSON stdout protocol documented at the top of this file — one JSON object per line for a host process to line-scan. The logger is silenced for the command's lifetime for exactly this reason: no stray log line may land on this channel.
raw ANSI terminal control (clear screen + scrollback) on transcript reset — an escape sequence, not a diagnostic.
the same raw terminal control at TUI startup; configureLogger({ level: 'silent' }) immediately above is what actually keeps a log line off this stream.
